name: Frontal-orbital advancement (frontal bossing / brow)

angle.text: In looksmaxxing usage, frontal-orbital advancement refers to surgery meant to push the brow ridge and upper orbital area forward for a more prominent brow and deeper-set eyes. The sources reviewed cover brow lifts and brow reduction rather than cosmetic advancement, so this specific goal is largely untested.

summary: A forward brow and forehead goal in looksmaxxing; the surgical literature found covers brow lifts and brow reduction, not cosmetic advancement.
note: No studies found on cosmetic advancement; related forehead surgery carries bone-healing and sinus risks per Wikipedia.
currentQuick:
Frontal-orbital advancement, as the term appears in looksmaxxing, means pushing the brow and upper orbit forward for a more projected look. Forum discussion found concerns brow lifts and combined surgery trips.
The closest documented literature is facial feminization surgery, which mostly reduces the brow ridge, and brow-lift studies.
How it works: Brow lifts change soft tissue position. Forehead contouring in feminization surgery grinds or reshapes bone over the frontal sinus. No source reviewed describes a cosmetic technique that advances the bone.
Risks and caveats: Wikipedia lists cranioplasty risks including improper bone healing, bone fragment movement and cyst formation, and thin sinus walls complicate grinding. Outcome data for forehead and orbit procedures are described as limited.
deepLead:
In looksmaxxing usage, frontal-orbital advancement and frontal bossing refer to surgery or other changes meant to push the brow ridge and upper orbital area forward, producing a more prominent forehead and brow. The sources reviewed contain little direct material on this exact aim.
The nearest documented surgical literature is facial feminization surgery, which usually reduces rather than advances the brow ridge and forehead , and brow-lift procedures that change eyebrow position rather than bone projection . No study of cosmetic frontal-orbital advancement in a non-craniofacial-condition population was found.

name: Ogee curve analysis

angle.text: The ogee curve is the S-shaped line from the cheekbone into the cheek hollow, used in aesthetic surgery as a filler goal and promoted online as a beauty marker. Forum users assess it in front and three-quarter photos to guide cheek treatments. Claims about it separating attractive from average faces are anecdotal.

summary: The S-shaped line from cheekbone to cheek hollow, used as a goal in filler surgery and as a hotly promoted beauty marker online.
note: Appears as a treatment goal in filler papers; no study tests it as a driver of attractiveness.
currentQuick:
The ogee curve is the S-shaped contour from the cheekbone into the hollow of the mid-cheek. Surgeons talk about restoring it in midface rejuvenation.
Looksmax.org members call it a major feature for attractiveness. No study tested that claim.
How it works: Forum members tie the curve to zygomatic projection, gonial flare and masseter size. Clinicians describe adjusting it with fillers or other midface volume treatments.
Risks and caveats: The concept itself is descriptive. Procedures used to pursue it, such as fillers or buccal fat removal, carry their own risks; forums also contain accounts of a self-performed buccal fat removal that went wrong.
deepLead:
In aesthetic facial surgery, the ogee curve describes the S-shaped line running from the cheekbone (malar prominence) down into the mid-cheek hollow . The word comes from geometry, where an ogee is an S-shaped curve joining a concave arc to a convex arc, and it is also used in architecture and engineering .
Mid-face rejuvenation in the surgical literature often aims to restore or smooth this curve . Filler papers describe a smooth ogee curve, along with an oval face, pronounced cheekbones and a defined jawline, as global aesthetic goals . On looksmax.org the curve is analyzed as a feature separating more attractive faces from average ones .

name: Canthopexy

chain: Lower lid sits tighter and higher
angle.text: Canthopexy tightens and repositions the lower eyelid without cutting the outer corner, and forum users discuss it for a firmer lid line and almond or fox-eye shape. The change is visible once healed. It is a routine companion to lower blepharoplasty, while its use for eye shape is untested.

summary: Lower-lid tendon tightening without cutting the corner; well-established in blepharoplasty, unproven as an eye-shape tool.
note: Published evidence concerns lid support in surgical patients; looksmaxxing durability claims are untested.
currentQuick:
Canthopexy anchors the lateral canthal tendon to lift and support the lower eyelid without cutting the lid margin. Surgeons use it with lower blepharoplasty to limit lid malposition.
Looksmaxxers discuss it for canthal tilt and almond eye shape, usually as an alternative to canthoplasty.
How it works: A suture secures the lateral canthal tendon to the orbital rim, giving the lower lid support and a slight lateral lift. Canthoplasty differs by cutting the canthus.
Risks and caveats: Surgical papers connect lower lid surgery with lid malposition and use canthal support to reduce that risk; ectropion prevention is itself a studied use. Forum members disagree about how long results last.
deepLead:
Canthopexy is a surgical procedure that tightens or repositions the lower eyelid by anchoring the lateral canthal tendon, without cutting the eyelid margin at the outer corner. Surgical papers present it as a routine companion to lower blepharoplasty that restores lid tone and contour and reduces the chance of lower lid malposition .
A 1993 paper argued canthopexy should be a routine part of or alternative to lower lid blepharoplasty , and a 10-year review of lower blepharoplasty with routine lateral canthal support reported on outcomes with that approach . In looksmaxxing communities it is discussed as a way to improve canthal tilt and eye shape, and is often compared with canthoplasty .

name: Tarsal strip procedure

chain: Lower lid anchored to orbital rim
angle.text: Forum users discuss the tarsal strip for tightening a lax lower eyelid and reducing sagging or visible white below the iris. The tighter lid is visible after healing. It is an established oculoplastic operation, with evidence mostly about lid function rather than cosmetic outcomes.

summary: A surgical lower-lid tightening technique from eyelid medicine that forum users discuss for sagging lids and scleral show; evidence is mostly functional, not cosmetic.
note: Surgical procedure; ectropion and lid retraction are recognised complications of lower-lid surgery in general.
currentQuick:
The tarsal strip (lateral tarsal strip) is an eyelid operation that shortens and re-anchors the outer end of a lax lower lid to the bone of the outer eye socket. It was described in 1979 for lids that sag, turn outward (ectropion) or turn inward (entropion).
In looksmaxxing discussion it is listed under hard-maxxing as a way to address a drooping lower lid and visible white below the iris (scleral show). Published studies mostly concern functional eyelid malposition and post-blepharoplasty complications rather than purely cosmetic goals.
How it works: Surgeons describe the problem as laxity or elongation of the lateral canthal tendon. A strip of tarsal plate at the outer lid is freed and fixed to the periosteum of the lateral orbital rim, tightening the lid margin against the eye.
Risks and caveats: Lower-lid surgery carries a risk of lid retraction, scleral show and ectropion, which is why tarsal strip and related tightening techniques are used in studies of preventing and treating these problems. As with any eyelid surgery, outcomes depend on pre-operative lid laxity and surgeon technique.
deepLead:
The tarsal strip procedure, or lateral tarsal strip, is an oculoplastic operation that tightens a lax lower eyelid by anchoring the outer end of the lid to the lateral orbital rim. It was published in 1979 as a technique for paralytic or senile upper and lower lid laxity, lateral canthal tendon laxity or malposition, and for scarring-related lid shortening problems after earlier lid-tightening surgery.
Its main medical uses are the correction of ectropion (outward-turning lid) and involutional entropion (inward-turning lid), and the prevention or treatment of lower lid malposition after lower-lid blepharoplasty. In looksmaxxing communities it is mentioned as a hard-maxxing option for a sagging lower lid and visible sclera beneath the iris.
The published literature consists mainly of case series, retrospective reviews and a few randomised trials in functional eyelid problems. No studies were found that evaluate the procedure specifically for cosmetic eye-shape goals in otherwise normal lids.

name: Medial epicanthoplasty

chain: Eye opens at the inner corner
angle.text: Medial epicanthoplasty removes or reduces the epicanthal fold over the inner eye corner to open up the eye, and is often paired with double eyelid surgery. The change is visible once healed. It is well described in the Asian blepharoplasty literature, mostly as case series.

summary: Surgery that releases or removes the inner-corner eyelid fold to open the eye; well described in the Asian blepharoplasty literature, mostly as case series.
note: Scarring at the inner corner is the main reported drawback; often combined with double eyelid surgery.
currentQuick:
Medial epicanthoplasty is a plastic-surgery procedure that modifies the epicanthal fold, the skin fold covering the inner corner of the eye. The fold is common in East Asian populations, and surgeons describe the operation as widening the visible inner eye and often performing it with double-eyelid surgery.
On looksmax.org, users have discussed it as a way to change inner-corner shape and perceived eye spacing, including planning surgery in Korea. Evidence consists of surgical case series and a few small trials.
How it works: Several techniques exist, including Z-plasty, Y-V advancement and skin-redraping methods, each rearranging skin at the medial canthus to release the fold and lengthen the horizontal opening of the eye.
Risks and caveats: The central concern in the literature is scarring at the inner corner; a randomised split-face trial tested botulinum toxin to reduce hypertrophic scars after the operation. Other reported issues include recurrence and asymmetry.
deepLead:
Medial epicanthoplasty is a cosmetic and reconstructive operation that reduces or removes the epicanthal fold, a vertical skin fold that partially covers the inner corner of the eye. The fold is particularly common in East Asian populations, where the epicanthal fold is described as frequently coexisting with a missing upper eyelid crease.
Epicanthoplasty is reported mainly in the context of Asian blepharoplasty, where it is frequently combined with creation of a double eyelid fold. Surgeons in published series describe the aim as exposing more of the medial canthus and lengthening the eye's horizontal dimension.
Many techniques have been published (Z-plasty and variants, Y-V advancement, skin redraping, root Z-epicanthoplasty). Reported evidence consists of retrospective series, an anatomical study and small trials, and scarring is the recurring concern.

name: Double eyelid surgery (Asian blepharoplasty)

angle.text: Double eyelid surgery forms an upper-lid crease for people who lack one, and is among the most commonly performed cosmetic procedures in East Asia. The crease and more open eye are visible after healing. The literature is large, though mostly case series rather than controlled trials.

summary: Surgery that creates an upper-lid crease; one of the most commonly performed cosmetic procedures in East Asia, with a large surgical literature but few controlled trials.
note: Static folds, asymmetry and need for revision are discussed in the literature.
currentQuick:
Double eyelid surgery creates a supratarsal fold, the crease in the upper lid that many East Asian eyelids lack. Surgeons describe incisional and suture-based approaches, and the procedure is often combined with epicanthoplasty.
Wikipedia describes it as among the most popular procedures in many East Asian countries, particularly South Korea, with operations typically lasting 30 to 60 minutes. Published evidence is mainly surgical case series, including patient-reported outcome measures such as FACE-Q.
How it works: The crease forms when the skin is attached to deeper lid structures such as the levator aponeurosis. Techniques include external incisions with fixation to the orbicularis, septum or aponeurosis, and buried sutures without a skin incision.
Risks and caveats: Literature describes static, overly depressed folds, multiple folds, asymmetry and failed folds requiring revision, plus suture-related problems with buried-suture methods.
deepLead:
Double eyelid surgery, also called Asian blepharoplasty or supratarsal fold creation, is an operation that forms a crease in the upper eyelid. Surgical authors note that Asian upper lids often have no superior palpebral fold, along with excess fat, pretarsal skin laxity and a medial epicanthal fold.
Wikipedia describes it as among the most popular cosmetic procedures in many East Asian countries, particularly South Korea, with typical operations lasting 30 to 60 minutes and sutures removed after 5 to 7 days. Authors in the plastic surgery literature say preferences for double eyelids have grown with cultural exchange.
Methods fall broadly into incisional and suture (non-incisional) approaches. Evidence is mostly retrospective surgical series; a FACE-Q validation study measured patient satisfaction in 200 cases.

name: Non-incisional double eyelid (suture method)

chain: Upper lid folds at the crease
angle.text: The suture method creates an upper-lid crease with buried stitches instead of an incision, and is popular in Asia, especially China. The crease is visible soon after the procedure. The literature focuses on how long the crease lasts and on suture complications.

summary: Buried-suture double eyelid surgery creates a crease with stitches instead of an incision; popular in Asia, with literature focused on crease loss and suture complications.
note: Crease loss, reoperation and suture-related eye complications are documented.
currentQuick:
The suture method forms an upper-lid crease by passing buried stitches through the lid so that skin is tethered to deeper tissue, without a skin incision. It is described as very popular in Asia, especially China.
Studies are retrospective and focus on how long creases last and on complications. Surgeons contrast it with the incision method, which involves a skin cut.
How it works: Sutures are placed through the eyelid at one or more points (for example two-point or continuous techniques) and buried, creating an adhesion that forms the crease line.
Risks and caveats: Reports describe suture exposure causing corneal damage, sometimes initially misdiagnosed, crease loss from suture loosening and reoperation, and suture-related complications needing removal.
deepLead:
Non-incisional (buried suture) double eyelid surgery creates an upper-lid crease by placing stitches through the lid rather than cutting skin. Surgical papers describe it as one of two alternative approaches, the other being the incision method, and as very popular in Asia, especially China.
Because it implants suture thread, authors say foreign-material complications must be considered. Recent literature examines crease loss, reoperation risk by age and fat removal, and eyebrow position changes.
The studies located are retrospective cohorts and case series.

name: Ptosis surgery (levator advancement)

angle.text: Ptosis repair raises a drooping upper eyelid, and forum users discuss the more open, more alert eye it produces. The lifted lid is visible after healing. It is primarily a functional operation supported by medical case series, with appearance benefit discussed mainly by patients.

summary: Surgery to raise a drooping upper lid, mainly a functional operation whose appearance benefit (a more open eye) is discussed on forums; supported in medical series.
note: Not purely cosmetic in origin; revision surgery and lid asymmetry are possible.
currentQuick:
Ptosis surgery lifts an upper eyelid that sits too low. Levator advancement tightens or reattaches the levator aponeurosis, the tendon that lifts the lid, and is a standard approach for aponeurotic (age- or stretch-related) ptosis.
Beyond vision, looksmaxxing users discuss it for a more open, alert-looking eye. One looksmax.org member shared a before-and-after account of a bilateral repair.
How it works: Surgeons choose among levator advancement or resection, Muller muscle-conjunctival resection and frontalis sling depending on cause and levator function.
Risks and caveats: Wikipedia lists uneven lids, dry eye, bleeding, infection and rarely loss of lid movement; one study cited there found about half of surgical patients needed more surgery within 8 to 10 years.
deepLead:
Ptosis surgery corrects drooping of the upper eyelid (blepharoptosis). Levator advancement, also called aponeurotic ptosis surgery, repairs the levator aponeurosis that has stretched or detached from the tarsal plate, and was described in the ophthalmic literature in 1979 with emphasis on preserving normal anatomy.
Ptosis may be minimal (1-2 mm), moderate (3-4 mm) or severe (over 4 mm), and may be congenital or acquired with myogenic, neurogenic, aponeurotic, mechanical or traumatic causes. Alternatives include Muller's muscle-conjunctival resection for mild ptosis with good levator function, and fascia lata for severe cases.
Evidence consists of case series, anatomy studies and functional-outcome studies, including one that linked vision-related impairment to surgery impact. Looksmaxxing forums discuss ptosis repair as a way to open the eye.

name: Oxymetazoline eye drops (Upneeq)

chain: Eyes look more open and awake
angle.text: Upneeq is a prescription oxymetazoline eye drop approved for acquired ptosis, used for a temporary lift of the upper lid that makes eyes look more open. Forum users also discuss nasal-spray substitutes, which are not the approved product. The lid lift is studied in ptosis trials.

summary: A prescription 0.1% oxymetazoline eye drop approved for acquired ptosis that lifts the lid slightly; forum users discuss cheaper nasal-spray substitutes, which are not the approved product.
note: Nasal-spray substitutes are not the approved eye formulation; ask a clinician.
currentQuick:
Upneeq is oxymetazoline hydrochloride 0.1% ophthalmic solution, approved by the FDA in July 2020 for acquired blepharoptosis in adults. Oxymetazoline is also long used in nasal decongestant sprays and redness eye drops.
Its appearance use is a brief lift of a mildly drooping upper lid for a more open look. On looksmax.org, users have asked whether nasal spray can substitute because Upneeq is costly and hard to obtain in Europe.
How it works: Oxymetazoline is an alpha-adrenergic agonist; for ptosis it is thought to stimulate receptors in Muller's muscle, which raises the lid.
Risks and caveats: Wikipedia describes rebound congestion and dependence with nasal oxymetazoline. Nasal spray is formulated for the nose, and clinicians' views on its use in the eye are not covered by the sources reviewed.
deepLead:
Upneeq is a brand of 0.1% oxymetazoline hydrochloride ophthalmic solution, approved by the US FDA in July 2020 to treat acquired blepharoptosis (drooping of the upper eyelid). Oxymetazoline is an imidazole-derivative alpha-adrenergic agonist developed from xylometazoline at Merck in 1961, and is also used in nasal sprays, redness drops and a rosacea cream.
For ptosis, the drug is thought to act on alpha receptors in Muller's muscle to lift the lid. It is also used, in published case reports, to manage eyelid ptosis after botulinum toxin treatment.
In looksmaxxing forums, Upneeq is discussed as a way to get a more open eye without surgery, and users discuss its cost and availability outside the US.

name: Eyelid tape / fold stickers

chain: Double eyelid or more open eye
angle.text: Eyelid tape and fold stickers create a temporary upper-lid crease, and many East Asian users wear them for a double eyelid look or to open hooded eyes. The effect is visible immediately and removable. It is the non-surgical counterpart to double eyelid surgery.

summary: Thin adhesive strips that press the upper lid into a temporary crease; a cosmetic stopgap with a small but real research literature on ocular effects.
note: A 2020 study of four weeks of daily wear examined effects on the front surface of the eye; research on long-term use is sparse.
currentQuick:
Eyelid tape and fold stickers are small adhesive strips, often crescent-shaped, placed on the upper eyelid so the skin folds into a visible crease. They are widely used by people with single (monolid) eyelids who want the look of a double eyelid without surgery. In looksmaxxing spaces the same tapes are also discussed as a way to lift a hooded or drooping lid.
The effect lasts only as long as the strip stays on. Published research on the product itself is limited to a few small studies and clinical reports.
How it works: The strip sticks to the lid skin and holds a fold in place above the lash line, imitating the crease that a levator attachment produces naturally. Clinically, a case report series has described the same type of tape being used to hold up a drooping lid in people with myotonic dystrophy type 1.
Risks and caveats: A 2020 study examined the front of the eye after four weeks of wear in young women with single eyelids. Skin irritation from adhesives and repeated lid stretching are commonly mentioned concerns in the cosmetic and plastic surgery literature, and a 2025 paper reviewed the implications of long-term use. Eyelid tape is a cosmetic product sold without prescription in most markets.
deepLead:
Eyelid tape, also sold as fold stickers or double eyelid tape, consists of thin adhesive strips applied to the upper eyelid to create a temporary crease. Many East Asians use the product to produce a double eyelid effect as a temporary means of increasing perceived beauty . It is the non-surgical counterpart to double eyelid surgery, which creates a permanent crease in people who do not have one naturally .
In looksmaxxing communities the tape is discussed both as a way to simulate a double eyelid and as a stopgap for droopy or hooded lids, including mild ptosis . Published research is limited: a small study examined ocular surface health after four weeks of wear , a clinical report has described the tape as an option for severe ptosis in myotonic dystrophy , and a 2025 article in Aesthetic Plastic Surgery discusses long-term use .

name: Eyelid glue

chain: Glue holds lid skin in a fold
angle.text: Users apply it to create a temporary double eyelid, giving a visible crease and a more open look for the day. It is used as a non-surgical alternative to double eyelid surgery. Published research on the product itself is limited.

summary: Cosmetic adhesive that sticks the lid skin into a temporary crease; little published research exists on the product itself.
note: Applied next to the eye; no studies specific to the glue were found.
currentQuick:
Eyelid glue is a cosmetic adhesive used to fix the upper lid skin into a fold, producing a temporary double eyelid. It serves the same goal as eyelid tape and is a non-surgical alternative to double eyelid surgery.
The sources reviewed contain no published studies of the glue itself, so what is known comes from background on double eyelid surgery and the cosmetic goal behind it.
How it works: A thin layer of adhesive holds a fold of lid skin in place so that a crease shows when the eye is open. The effect lasts until the glue is removed or wears off.
Risks and caveats: No clinical studies of eyelid glue were found. Any adhesive used next to the eye raises general questions of skin and eye irritation, which have not been specifically studied for these products in the sources reviewed.
deepLead:
Eyelid glue is a cosmetic adhesive applied to the upper eyelid to hold the skin in a fold, giving the appearance of a double eyelid for a limited time. It is a non-surgical alternative to double eyelid surgery, which creates a permanent crease .
No published clinical studies of eyelid glue were located. This article therefore describes the aesthetic context only and does not assess the product's effects.

name: Canthal tilt tape (lateral eye lift tape)

chain: Tape pulls outer corner to temple
angle.text: Looksmaxxers use it to lift the outer eye corners for a more upward-angled, positive canthal tilt look while it is worn. The change in angle is visible straight away; no studies on the tape were found.

summary: Tape pulled toward the temple to angle the outer eye corners upward; no studies were found.
note: No clinical research found; applied next to the eye.
currentQuick:
Canthal tilt tape is adhesive tape stuck near the outer corner of the eye and pulled back toward the temple, so the outer corner sits higher. In looksmaxxing vocabulary a more upward-angled outer corner is called positive canthal tilt.
The sources reviewed contain no studies of the tape. This entry therefore covers definitions only.
How it works: The tape holds the skin at the lateral canthus under tension, which is intended to raise the apparent position of the outer corner relative to the inner corner. The effect is temporary and ends when the tape is removed.
Risks and caveats: No studies of safety or effectiveness were found. Adhesive and skin tension near the eye are general considerations that have not been tested for this product.
deepLead:
Canthal tilt tape, also called lateral eye lift tape, is a temporary cosmetic aid in which tape is attached near the outer eye corner and pulled toward the temple to alter the apparent angle of the eye. The canthi are the corners of the eye where the upper and lower lids meet; the lateral canthus is the outer corner and the medial canthus the inner corner .
No published clinical studies of the tape were located. In appearance forums a more upward-angled outer corner is commonly called positive canthal tilt, but the sources reviewed for this entry do not provide data on perceptions of tilt or on the tape.

name: Winged eyeliner for tilt

angle.text: The wing is drawn to suggest an upturned outer eye corner, giving the eyes a more tilted, defined shape as soon as it is applied. It is a standard makeup technique; its effect on perceived tilt has not been formally studied.

summary: Extending liner outward and upward to suggest a more tilted outer eye corner; a makeup technique with no studies on its effect on perceived tilt.
note: No studies of the technique's effect on perceived canthal tilt were found.
currentQuick:
Winged eyeliner is a makeup technique in which the line along the upper lashes is extended past the outer corner of the eye. In looksmaxxing communities it is discussed as a way to imitate a positive canthal tilt, an outer eye corner sitting higher than the inner.
The technique is a long-standing makeup style. No published research was found on whether it changes how tilted the eyes look.
How it works: A dark line is drawn along the upper lash line and flicked outward and upward, so the eye is visually extended in that direction. The result is an optical illusion created with pigment.
Risks and caveats: Eyeliner is a standard cosmetic. Product quality varies by region, and the FDA has described traditional kohl as unsafe over lead concerns. Winged liner is typically worn with ordinary pencil or liquid liners.
deepLead:
Winged eyeliner defines the upper lid and extends the line outward to a point about halfway toward the end of the eyebrow. A related style, cat eye, uses a thicker wing that runs along both upper and lower lash lines .
In looksmaxxing discussions the wing is mentioned as a cosmetic way to suggest a positive canthal tilt. The sources reviewed contain no studies of how liner affects perceived eye tilt.

name: Tightlining / waterline liner

chain: Lash line looks darker and denser
Eyes look deeper and more defined
angle.text: Users apply liner at the waterline to make lashes look fuller and the eyes look more defined, visible immediately. It is popular in makeup and grooming circles; its effect on perceived eye depth has not been studied.

summary: Liner applied at the lash roots or waterline to darken the lash line; no studies on its effect on perceived eye depth.
note: No research found on appearance effects; waterproof products are commonly used.
currentQuick:
Tightlining is a makeup technique in which liner is applied right against the lash roots, under the upper lashes and above the lower lashes, so lashes look fuller and the lash line darker. Waterline liner is applied to the inner rim of the lid.
In looksmaxxing talk it is mentioned as a way to make eyes look defined or deeper-set. No studies of that claim were found.
How it works: Dark pigment fills the gaps between lashes and at the lid margin, which can make lashes look denser and longer. Waterproof products are commonly preferred for this technique.
Risks and caveats: Liner placed at the lid margin sits very close to the eye surface. No studies on the technique were found in the sources reviewed.
deepLead:
Tightlining is a method of eyeliner application in which liner is placed close to the waterline, under the upper lashes and above the lower lashes. Waterproof products are usually preferred, and the technique can make lashes appear longer .
Proponents in appearance communities say it defines the eyes and suggests depth. No published research was found on how tightlining changes perceived eye shape or attractiveness.

name: Guyliner / kohl

angle.text: Men use eyeliner or kohl to make the eyes look darker and more intense, an effect visible as soon as it is applied. The style runs from ancient Egyptian use to 2000s emo guyliner. Appearance effects are observable rather than trial-tested.

summary: Eyeliner worn by men, from ancient kohl to 2000s emo guyliner; discussed for an intense look, with documented lead concerns about some traditional kohl.
note: The FDA considers traditional kohl unsafe because of possible lead content.
currentQuick:
Guyliner is a term for eyeliner worn by men. Kohl, a soft dark powder, is among the oldest eye cosmetics and was worn by Egyptian men and women of all classes. In looksmaxxing talk men's liner is mentioned for a more intense or hunter-eyed look.
No research was found on how liner changes perceived attractiveness in men. The best-documented issue is lead in some traditional kohl.
How it works: Dark pigment placed along the lash line increases contrast around the eye and can make the eye look larger or more defined. Traditional kohl was made from stibnite or galena; Western products generally use carbon or charcoal.
Risks and caveats: Studies since the early 1990s have found high lead levels in some kohl products, and lead exposure has been linked to anemia and developmental effects, though some research disputes the links. The FDA does not list kohl as an approved color additive and considers it unsafe, with import and sale in the US illegal. Western commercial eyeliners generally use other pigments.
deepLead:
Kohl is a soft, usually black powder used around the eyes. Traditional kohl was made by grinding stibnite (antimony sulfide), and many modern and homemade versions use galena (lead sulfide); Western manufacturers generally use carbon or charcoal . Egyptians of all social classes are reported to have worn it from about 3100 BCE, and both men and women appear in tomb depictions .
The term guyliner describes men who wear eyeliner and became popular in the early 2000s emo scene, partly through bands such as Fall Out Boy and Panic! at the Disco . In appearance forums, men's eyeliner is mentioned as a way to look more intense. No studies were found on this effect, while research on lead in some traditional kohl is described below.

name: Eyelash growth serum (peptide, OTC)

angle.text: Users apply these drug-free serums hoping for longer, thicker lashes that frame the eyes. They are popular in forums and sold as alternatives to prescription prostaglandin products. Published trials of the peptide versions were not found.

summary: Drug-free cosmetic serums for lash length; popular in forums, but no published trials of the peptide versions.
note: Not the same as prescription bimatoprost (Latisse); trial data exist only for the latter.
currentQuick:
Peptide lash serums are over-the-counter products applied to the lash line to make lashes look longer or fuller. They are often positioned as non-prescription alternatives to Latisse.
Forum users ask for brand recommendations and report mixed results. No published human trials of the peptide products were found.
How it works: Manufacturers describe peptides and conditioning ingredients as supporting lash growth or condition. Prescription bimatoprost, by contrast, is a prostaglandin analogue with documented lash effects.
Risks and caveats: Evidence on specific safety profiles of peptide serums is limited. Eye-area products carry general irritation risks; prescription bimatoprost has documented effects such as redness and eyelid darkening.
deepLead:
Over-the-counter eyelash growth serums are cosmetic liquids or gels applied along the lash line with the aim of making eyelashes look longer, thicker or fuller. Many are marketed as drug-free alternatives to prescription prostaglandin products, and typically list peptides, conditioning agents, botanical extracts or vitamins as their active ingredients rather than a prostaglandin analogue.
Lashes behave differently from scalp hair: according to Wikipedia, their length is largely genetically set, the number of follicles cannot increase after birth, and length, thickness and darkness decline with age. The same article notes that some cosmetic brands use peptides instead of prostaglandins because of regulatory rules in places such as Canada and California.
No published human trial of a peptide-based lash serum was identified in the research used for this article, so claims about their effect rest on manufacturer statements and user reports. On looksmax.org the products are discussed alongside prescription bimatoprost (Latisse), castor oil, rosemary oil and minoxidil.

name: Lash extensions

angle.text: Users get them for longer, fuller, curled lashes that make the eyes look larger and more defined, a change visible as soon as they are applied. A set typically lasts a few weeks. The result is cosmetic and observable directly.

summary: Salon-applied individual lashes bonded to your own for length and fullness, lasting a few weeks per set.
note: Adhesive fumes have been linked to respiratory problems in technicians.
currentQuick:
Lash extensions are individual false lashes glued onto natural lashes by a technician. They add length, curl and density and last roughly three to four weeks.
Styles range from natural-looking classic sets to fuller volume sets.
How it works: Each synthetic lash is attached to a single natural lash with cyanoacrylate-type adhesive, and falls out as the natural lash sheds.
Risks and caveats: A case report linked the glue to occupational asthma and rhinitis in technicians. Licensing rules vary by jurisdiction. Few clinical studies examine client outcomes.
deepLead:
Lash extensions are individual synthetic (or sometimes natural-material) lashes attached by a technician to a person's own lashes with semi-permanent adhesive, to add length, curl and fullness. According to Wikipedia, an application typically takes up to two hours and lasts about three to four weeks depending on care.
Styles are commonly described as classic (the most natural), volume (the fullest) and hybrid (a mix). The technician customises material, length, colour and curvature to the client's eyes.
The adhesives commonly contain cyanoacrylate, and published case reports have linked the fumes to occupational asthma and rhinitis in lash technicians.

name: Lash tint

angle.text: Users get lashes dyed so they look darker and fuller without mascara, a visible change for several weeks. It is a common salon service. The effect is cosmetic and directly observable.

summary: Salon dye to darken lashes; regulators in the US say no dyes are approved for the eye area.
note: The FDA warns against dyeing lashes and brows and cites eye injuries.
currentQuick:
Lash tinting darkens eyelashes with dye so they appear fuller without mascara. It is offered as a salon service.
There is very little published research on it.
How it works: A dye is applied to the lashes and stains the hair itself, so the colour lasts until lashes shed.
Risks and caveats: The FDA says hair dyes should not be used on eyelashes or eyebrows and that no color additives are approved for that use, citing reports of eye injury.
deepLead:
Lash tinting is a salon procedure in which a dye is applied to eyelashes to darken them, so they look fuller without mascara. Wikipedia lists tints, alongside extensions, among popular salon eyelash procedures.
In the United States, the FDA states that hair dyes should not be used on eyebrows or eyelashes, and that no color additives are approved for dyeing them. The agency cites reports of eye injuries, including blindness, from hair dyes used near the eyes.
No published clinical studies of lash tinting were identified, and little other source material is available.

name: Eyebrow growth serum

angle.text: Users apply peptide or botanical serums hoping to make sparse brows look denser and fuller, often alongside castor oil, microneedling or minoxidil. Published evidence centres on prescription bimatoprost rather than the over-the-counter products.

summary: Peptide and botanical brow serums are popular online; published evidence centres on prescription bimatoprost, not the OTC products.
note: Studies of bimatoprost for brows do not apply to peptide serums.
currentQuick:
Eyebrow growth serums are topical products sold to make brows look denser. Many contain peptides or plant extracts.
Research mostly concerns prescription bimatoprost; one 2019 paper studied a botanical extract.
How it works: Makers and forum users describe peptides as stimulating hair-follicle activity. No trials of those peptide serums for brows were found.
Risks and caveats: Eye-area products can irritate. Bimatoprost, a prescription drug, has its own documented effects such as eyelid darkening.
deepLead:
Eyebrow growth serums are topical cosmetic products, often containing peptides or botanical extracts, marketed to make sparse brows look denser or fuller. They are discussed in looksmaxxing communities alongside castor oil, microneedling, minoxidil and prescription prostaglandin analogues.
Published evidence specific to over-the-counter serums is thin. A 2019 paper in Clinical, Cosmetic and Investigational Dermatology reported on a plant-derived extract (Jarilla-Coffea) described as improving eyelash and eyebrow growth in women. Studies of bimatoprost, a prescription prostaglandin analogue, have examined its use on eyebrows.

name: Castor oil on brows/lashes

chain: Oil brushed on brows and lashes
Hair believed to thicken or lengthen
angle.text: Practitioners brush castor oil on brows and lashes as a folk remedy for thicker, longer hair, and it is popular online. The growth claim has not been tested in trials; anecdote drives its use.

summary: Folk remedy of brushing castor oil on brows and lashes for thickness; popular online, untested in trials.
note: No trials identified; keep oil out of the eyes.
currentQuick:
Castor oil is a thick plant oil that many people brush onto brows and lashes hoping for thicker hair.
Forum users report both positive and underwhelming results.
How it works: Proponents attribute effects to ricinoleic acid and conditioning; no study has tested this for brows or lashes.
Risks and caveats: Topical use is generally described as low risk, but eye-area products can irritate.
deepLead:
Applying castor oil to eyebrows and eyelashes is a folk remedy that practitioners say thickens or lengthens them. Castor oil is pressed from castor beans and consists mostly of triglycerides, with ricinoleic acid making up most of its fatty acids.
Wikipedia's castor oil article lists laxative, skin-care and industrial uses and does not describe hair, brow or lash growth claims or evidence. No clinical studies on the practice were identified.
